title: Divergence of the Iteration x_{n+1} = x_n^2 + 1
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Starting from x_0 = 2, iterate the rule x_{n+1} = x_n^2 + 1. Compute the first few terms and prove rigorously that the sequence grows at least geometrically and therefore diverges to infinity.

steps.title: Generate the First Terms
steps.explanation: Repeated application of the rule turns the modest seed 2 into rapidly widening numbers, hinting at faster-than-linear growth.
steps.why: Explicit computation of an orbit is the standard first probe of any discrete dynamical system.

steps.title: Prove Monotone Increase
steps.explanation: Completing the square shows the gap between successive terms is always strictly positive, so the sequence climbs at every single step.
steps.why: A sum of a square and a positive constant can never vanish or turn negative, whatever x_n is.

steps.title: Establish a Geometric Lower Bound
steps.explanation: Every orbit point from the seed 2 onward is at least 2, and for such values the next term doubles at minimum: x_{n+1} = x_n^2 + 1 >= 2 x_n.
steps.why: Induction seals the estimate: the seed satisfies x_0 >= 2, and the rule x^2 + 1 > x for x >= 2 keeps all later terms in the region where doubling holds.

steps.title: Conclude Divergence to Infinity
steps.explanation: Telescoping the doubling inequalities bounds the sequence below by an exponentially growing power of 2, which exceeds every real threshold.
steps.why: By the comparison principle, any sequence dominating a divergent-to-infinity sequence must itself diverge to infinity; numerically 677^2 + 1 = 458330 already confirms the surge.
